content.value_statement: Teams need quick patterns for Log Analytics and Azure Monitor metrics. This skill provides Python examples for LogsQueryClient, MetricsQueryClient, Kusto queries, and result handling.
actual_capabilities: Shows how to install the Azure Monitor Query Python package.
Demonstrates DefaultAzureCredential authentication for Azure SDK clients.
Provides Log Analytics workspace query examples with Kusto statements.
Provides Azure Monitor metrics queries with granularity and aggregations.
Shows batch log queries, partial result handling, and DataFrame conversion.
Includes async client patterns for logs and metrics queries.
limitations: Requires valid Azure credentials and permissions before queries can run.
Does not create workspaces, resources, dashboards, or alerts.
Does not validate arbitrary Kusto query cost, scope, or performance.
Examples may need package imports and variable values added in real projects.

use_cases.title: Investigate application errors
use_cases.description: Use Log Analytics examples to inspect requests, exceptions, slow operations, and status code trends.

use_cases.title: Analyze operational metrics
use_cases.description: Query Azure resource metrics with time ranges, granularity, and aggregation settings.

use_cases.title: Build monitoring automation
use_cases.description: Use batch, async, and DataFrame patterns as a starting point for Python monitoring jobs.

prompt_templates.title: Run a basic log query
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner setup for a single workspace query.
prompt_templates.prompt: Show me a Python pattern to query Log Analytics requests from the last hour with LogsQueryClient.

prompt_templates.title: Query metrics for one resource
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate metrics retrieval for an Azure resource.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a Python example that queries CPU and network metrics for an Azure resource over one hour.

prompt_templates.title: Handle partial query results
prompt_templates.scenario: Operational logging workflow with error handling.
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me handle partial and failed Log Analytics responses while keeping useful rows for investigation.

prompt_templates.title: Design async monitoring automation
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced automation with async clients and batching.
prompt_templates.prompt: Design an async workflow that batches two Log Analytics queries, handles partial results, and closes clients correctly.

output_examples.input: Query recent application request failures from Log Analytics.
output_examples.output: A focused Python plan using LogsQueryClient, a one hour timespan, a Kusto filter for failed requests, and status handling.

output_examples.input: Read CPU metrics for an Azure virtual machine.
output_examples.output: A metrics query outline that authenticates, reads the resource URI, requests Percentage CPU, applies five minute granularity, and summarizes averages.

output_examples.input: Compare exceptions and slow requests in one workflow.
output_examples.output: A batch query approach that runs separate Kusto statements, checks each response, and prepares rows for analysis.

best_practices: Use narrow time ranges and filters before increasing query scope.
Handle partial results and failures before using returned tables.
Close async clients and credentials after asynchronous queries complete.
anti_patterns: Running broad workspace queries without time limits or filters.
Printing sensitive log fields without redaction or access review.
Assuming metric names, namespaces, and dimensions are identical across resources.

faq.question: Does this skill run Azure queries automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides examples and guidance. Users must run code with their own Azure credentials.

faq.question: Which Azure clients does it cover?
faq.answer: It covers LogsQueryClient and MetricsQueryClient, including async variants.

faq.question: Can it help with Kusto queries?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes common Kusto examples for requests, exceptions, slow requests, and top errors.

faq.question: Does it require environment variables?
faq.answer: The examples use environment variables for workspace IDs and resource URIs. Projects can use other configuration methods.

faq.question: Can it convert results for analysis?
faq.answer: Yes. It shows converting a returned table into a pandas DataFrame.

faq.question: Is this a full monitoring solution?
faq.answer: No. It is a reference skill for Python query patterns, not a dashboard or alerting system.
